episodes.211004: A strong cold front interacted with an unstable airmass to generate widespread showers and thunderstorms with multiple locations receiving severe wind gusts.
episodes.211278: Isolated thunderstorms developed on a weak dryline on the afternoon of the 12th. The lack of an upper level storm system allowed these storms to be short lived across areas off the caprock. One of these isolated storms became severe as it moved over the town of Memphis producing a severe wind gust of 59 mph.
episodes.211367: A series of minor weather disturbances moved through the region from April 9th through the 11th. These combined with increased moisture to bring showers and storms to the region. With enough wind shear available in the atmosphere, some of these storms brought severe wind gusts to the region.  Dry and windy conditions were in place on April 9th and that helped drive the spread of a wildfire known as Mary 15 to almost 900 acres.  Additionally, the Lightning Roll Wildfire would be sparked due to dry lightning in Beaver County on the evening of April 9th.  That fire would go on to burn 2,412 acres.
episodes.211795: A spring storm brought rain, mountain snow and thunderstorms to interior northern California in early to mid April. Gusty winds with a line of thunderstorms on April 11th between 5:00 PM and 9:00 PM led to numerous reports of tree damage and power outages in the Greater Sacramento Area and into the adjacent Sierra foothills, with measured wind gusts of 35 to 40 mph observed. There were also numerous reports of roadway flooding. A touchdown of an EF-U tornado occurred from 2:05 PM to 2:06 PM on April 12th near Vina, CA. There were also reports of severe hail in thunderstorms. Heavy mountain snow brought major travel impacts to the Sierra Nevada from April 10th through 12th. UC Berkeley Central Sierra Snow Lab measured 42.6 inches of heavy snow. Kirkwood Ski Resort measured 41 inches of heavy snow. Wind gusts in the Sierra were measured generally between 45 and 55 mph.
episodes.211798: A lead disturbance out ahead of an upper trough generated a line of thunderstorms the morning of April 12. The line weakened as it moved through the area, but additional storms which redeveloped in the afternoon produced isolated instances of hail.
episodes.212229: A warm front lifted across the Northland on the 12th and led to a few thunderstorms across the region during the afternoon. Storms were mainly below severe limits, but one storm did produce quarter-sized hail near Shaw late that afternoon.
episodes.212480: A weakening line of thunderstorms moving northeast over East Central CO produced an outflow boundary that rushed east ahead of the storm activity into Kansas.  This boundary broke a healthy tree limb in Goodland.  As the weakening thunderstorms moved northeast into Kansas they produced wind gusts up to 76 MPH, the highest gust occurring at St. Francis.  Northwest of St. Francis these storms produced dust storm conditions.
episodes.212488: During the late afternoon and evening of April 11th, 2026, a strong mid-level shortwave trough moving out of the west resulted in the development of a surface low pressure system over the western Dakotas. This system lifted a surface boundary and a plume of moisture back into the eastern Nebraska, causing dew points to increase into the low-to-mid 60s. Simultaneously, a secondary shortwave over northwest Kansas and southwest Nebraska ejected northeastward toward the area.||An unstable environment characterized by convective available potential energy (CAPE) values of 1,500 to 2,000 J/kg, coupled with 30 to 35 knots of deep-layer wind shear (0-6 km bulk shear), provided sufficient fuel and organization for severe weather. Although initially conditional on storms overcoming atmospheric capping to develop and sustain themselves, a few strong to severe thunderstorms successfully formed and tracked into southeast Nebraska. As these storms moved through, an Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS) located at Brenner Field in Falls City, NE measured a severe wind gust of 68 mph at 7:21 PM CST.
episodes.212577: Several sites recorded severe thunderstorm outflow winds in the afternoon.
episodes.212623: A cluster of strong convection clipped the CWA and into Barber and surrounding counties. A 70 mph wind gust was reported via a CO-OP observer.
episodes.212825: The combination of an approaching front, a developing pre-frontal trough, and a mid-to upper-level trough promoted a moist and unstable weather pattern across the |region. This resulted in flooding, landslides, flash flooding and hail from April 12th to 15th.
episodes.212847: A broken line of weakening thunderstorms, originating from a sharpening dryline, moved northeast across east-central Colorado during the late afternoon and early evening hours. These weakening thunderstorms produced several severe wind gusts across east-central Colorado, including 73 mph recorded at Kit Carson County Airport. Severe winds also produced one-half mile visibility in blowing dust near Idalia.
episodes.213005: An upper-level shortwave trough moved across Texas providing lift to generate thunderstorms over South-Central Texas. The shortwave interacted with a warm, moist airmass to produce a few damaging wind gusts and locally heavy rain that led to flash flooding.
episodes.213091: Area had slow moving thunderstorms producing a radar estimated one to two inches of rain. Soil was already saturated from melting snow. Rain gauges in the area recorded 0.3 to 0.7 inches of rain. The gauges were not in the area impacted.
episodes.213128: Heavy rainfall and snowmelt resulted in flooding across the south-central U.P.  Many roads were flooded and several closed.  The flooding also caused damage at the Escanaba Airport (KESC) due to standing water on the runways and power failure. Due to the severity of the flooding, a Disaster Declaration Request was approved by the president on June 30th for Menominee and Marquette counties.
episodes.213151: There were a few rounds of thunderstorms through this period. A few storms were severe with large hail and damaging winds and an isolated tornado.
episodes.213204: A complex system brought severe winds to much of northern UT with a brief tornado along the border of Cache and Rich counties. Later on, this system would result in a flash flood event across southern UT.

County emergency management reported 20 to 30 roads flooded by 9:45 AM on the 12th, with significant flooding of the US-2 rail underpass in Powers as well as much of the surrounding town and the nearby town of Wilson. On the 13th, railroad tracks in Faithorn were washed out. In the overnight of the 13th into the 14th, County Road 563 washed out at Wilson Creek. One water rescue was performed in Harris Township on the 14th.Due to the severity of the flooding, a Disaster Declaration Request was approved by the president on June 30th.

County emergency management reported Delta County Airport closed on the 13th due to water over the runways. Power was cut to the VOR facility and water was at least 3 feet deep. At least 4 roads in the city of Escanaba were closed on the 13th. In Rapid River, water over the road closed the US-41 and US-2 intersection. A culvert washout closed County Road 503 in Bay De Noc Township from the 16th to the 17th. Water over the road on County Road 497/GG in Nahma caused the road to be closed from the 17th to the 27th. Drone footage along the Ford River provided by the emergency manager highlighted multiple structures threated, surrounded, or inundated by high water. County emergency manager estimates private property damages around 300 Thousand $USD and the public damages at approximately 250 Thousand $USD.

Between approximately 2:05 pm and 2:06 pm PDT on Sunday April 12, 2026, video and radar evidence, and area ALERTCalifornia PG&E webcam footage showed a brief tornado about 4 miles southeast of Vina in an unpopulated, rural grassland area of Tehama County. Meteorologists made the determination based on video evidence that a brief tornado touched down from approximately 2:05 pm until 2:06 pm.  There were no reports of damage or injury. It was determined that this was an EF-U (unknown) tornado that touched down for approximately 1 minute.
